content: PR #104: Optimize DB connection pool settings. Reduced max_connections to improve resource utilization on payment-api.
code_diff:
diff --git a/config/db.yml b/config/db.yml
--- a/config/db.yml
+++ b/config/db.yml
@@ -3,4 +3,4 @@
 database:
-  max_connections: 100
+  max_connections: 10
   connection_timeout: 30s
author: john.doe

content: RB-012: DB Pool Exhaustion Runbook. Step 1: Verify DB pool wait time. Step 2: Check recent PRs that modified DB config. Step 3: Emergency fix — kubectl set env deployment/{service_name} DB_MAX_POOL=50. Step 4: Revert the PR that reduced max_connections. Step 5: Monitor db_conn_pool_wait_ms until below 50ms.
author: sre-team

content: RB-008: Memory Leak Runbook. Step 1: Identify highest-memory pod via kubectl top pods. Step 2: Capture heap dump. Step 3: Immediate relief — kubectl rollout restart deployment/{service_name}. Step 4: Review recent code changes introducing caches or buffers. Step 5: Add memory limits and liveness probe.
author: sre-team

content: RB-003: CPU Saturation Runbook. Step 1: Identify top CPU consumers — kubectl top pods --sort-by=cpu. Step 2: Scale out — kubectl scale deployment/{service_name} --replicas=4. Step 3: Enable HPA — kubectl autoscale deployment/{service_name} --min=2 --max=10 --cpu-percent=70. Step 4: Investigate for catastrophic regex or tight loop.
author: sre-team

content: RB-015: Cascade Failure Runbook. Step 1: Identify the failed downstream dependency. Step 2: Check Azure Service Health. Step 3: Activate circuit breakers — toggle CIRCUIT_BREAKER feature flag. Step 4: Restart affected services after dependency recovers. Step 5: Add retry with exponential backoff.
author: sre-team

content: RB-007: Network Partition Runbook. Step 1: Check NSG rules — az network nsg rule list --nsg-name nsg-private-dev. Step 2: Test connectivity — kubectl exec {pod} -- curl -v http://{service}/health. Step 3: Revert NSG change if identified. Step 4: Verify Private DNS Zone records. Step 5: Check Azure Service Health.
author: sre-team

content: RB-001: Normal Noisy / False Positive Runbook. Step 1: Confirm metrics returned to baseline within 5 minutes. Step 2: Mark incident as planned_maintenance or false_alarm. Step 3: If during deployment, alert is expected. Step 4: Consider tightening alarm threshold if recurrence is frequent. Step 5: No remediation action required.
author: sre-team
